ext_01.rationale: Establishes a deep two-variable CM elliptic analogue of the Coleman-Ihara formula with rigorous semilocal Coleman-theoretic machinery, accurate algebraic identities (such as Proposition 3.8 and Lemmas 4.8-4.11), and exemplary scholarly grounding (including noting the Darmon-Lauder-Rotger correction and concurrent work [SV26]). Minor weaknesses are that compatibility across levels m in Definition 4.12 is not explicitly proved (notably when i=1 and 1 - pi^(j-1) pi_bar^(i-1) is not a p-adic unit), and Sections 3-4 rely heavily on imported propositions without independent special-case or computational checks. Overall, this is a strong, well-calibrated research contribution suitable for a high-level number theory journal.

ext_02.rationale: Investigates attractive inverse-power Schrodinger potentials via the log-coordinate substitution, correctly obtaining two elementary E=0 exact solutions (n = 6 - 2D and n = 2D - 2) and basic WKB asymptotics. However, the manuscript has major mathematical and conceptual flaws: it mistakes eigenvalues of the non-self-adjoint adjoint operator (varying the extension parameter v) for a continuous bound-state spectrum, falsely claims E_GS = 0 for the 3D hard-core n=2 potential at U_0 = 0.33, r_0 = 0.001 due to a numerical cutoff artifact contradicting exact scale invariance, and introduces a spurious +du/dx term in the 2D vortex equation (30). It also conflates unrelated cavity-QED collapse-and-revival papers [12-17], omits foundational singular-potential and Bessel-solution literature (e.g., Case; Frank-Land-Spector), and suffers from numerous typos and mis-referenced equations.

ext_03.rationale: Proves the first linear upper bound chi'_rn(G) <= 3 chi'(G) for all loopless multigraphs via an inventive total edge-dominating almost-star forest and 2-degenerate conflict-graph argument, alongside exact values for K_{m,n} and K_n and the star-forest structure of optimal colorings of K_n. Every proof and construction examined (including parallel-edge multigraph cases, the counting argument in Lemma 2.6, the sporadic obstructions K_{2,2}, K_4, K_6, and Construction I in Lemma 3.10) is airtight, self-contained, and written with exceptional clarity, complemented by the sharp B_1 = K_3 example (Example 2.5). While purely deductive without formal or computational verification artifacts, its structural depth, elegance, and complete rigor make it readily publishable in a top-tier combinatorics journal.

ext_04.rationale: Completely characterizes the submonoid generated by lazy and invertible cellular automata over C_2 x C_2 with binary alphabet, proving exact membership, cardinality (59,712), relative rank 1, and the unique maximal proper submonoid (|Q| = 65,024) via crisp, self-contained algebraic proofs independent of enumeration. Verification and calibration are gold-standard: independent C++ BFS and Python certificate checks prove exactness of |D| = 4,007 and shortest-word lengths, a kernel-checked Lean 4 formalization (no sorry or native_decide) verifies the criterion and cardinalities, and open gaps (a structural criterion for D) are stated transparently. Its primary limitation for a top-tier general journal is its narrow scope—a single order-4 group following the general finite classification already established in [2]—together with a small reference list.

ext_05.rationale: Proves an exact Poisson-summation identification, full positivity and inertia classification (Theorem 1), covariance-independent exponential trace-norm and fidelity bounds (Theorem 2), and rescaled sqrt(d) basis-coherence limits (Theorem 4) for signed Wigner discrete-variable Gaussian states in all odd dimensions d >= 3. The analytic proofs in Appendices A-D check out accurately and are reinforced by strong independent verification (elementary rational negative-direction bounds, rational interval certification of eps_31 < 1/16000, and 192-bit Arb enclosures), with notably honest calibration distinguishing proved state/basis limits from numerical coherent-frame comparisons. Main weaknesses are uneven exposition—pairing elementary tight-frame background in Sections II and V with highly compressed proofs in Appendices A-C and minor notation shifts (sigma_ij vs a,b,c)—and restriction to centered single-mode states.

ext_06.rationale: Proposition 1 validly combines defensive-mixture importance sampling with betting supermartingales and Ville's inequality, backed by exact brute-force enumeration and 9,840 replications with preregistered falsifiers and candid reporting of negative outcomes (including failure on the narrow (4,7) tree and uncompetitive unenumerated upper bounds). However, Equation (2) drops the 1/9 bet-grid mixture factor—causing Section 5.5 to misattribute most of the observed ~2x upper-bound threshold gap—and Section 3.4 reuses weight notation loosely. Methodological novelty is incremental and the evaluation is confined to tiny GPT-2 trees (L <= 7, coarse token classes) where gains already degrade at L = 7, limiting significance for realistic LLM safety evaluation.

ext_07.rationale: The paired potential-outcome design, independent pilot/tuning/evaluation namespaces, and finite-sample Hoeffding simultaneous bounds over all 45 contrasts are mathematically accurate and unusually well calibrated in their caveats. However, the study merely audits an uncited earlier toy simulation with blatantly broken baselines in a restrictive homogeneous Gaussian K=33, T=66 setting, offering no new algorithm, no theoretical analysis, and no comparison against standard fixed-budget best-arm identification methods. Literature grounding is severely inadequate—citing only one external paper (Karnin et al., 2013) without implementing it and omitting the vast fixed-budget BAI and ranking-and-selection literatures.

ext_08.rationale: This paper cleanly resolves Krishnan's Conjecture 5 for P(n,3) (n >= 13) and establishes the sharp stabilization threshold Z(P(n,4)) = 10 (n >= 18) plus all smaller values via an airtight forcing-sources boundary lemma, buffered empty-column deletion, and exact slot-score or bounded-circumference reductions. Verification is exemplary—combining a standalone C99 checker, a Lean 4 formalization of the k=3 stabilization theorem with module blob provenance, and 100 freshly replayed DRAT-trim proofs with an independent semantic checker—paired with candid disclosure of the unlogged #print axioms audit and unformalized k=4 case. Significance is bounded primarily by the heavy SAT dependence for k=4 (with no structural proof or general-k extension), though the paper is publication-ready for a top combinatorics journal.

ext_09.rationale: Completely resolves an explicitly posed open problem from IEEE Transactions on Information Theory (Singhvi et al., 2025) by proving that alternating words uniquely maximize posterior input entropy for two deletions (n >= 1) and two insertions (n >= 5), alongside exact all-radius insertion histograms and the three-deletion histogram for alternating words. The human-checkable proofs—using an exact first-symbol run recurrence, tight strict-convexity estimates, mask-component grouping, and exact arbitrary-precision integer certificates Q(y) without floating-point filtering—are remarkably clean, rigorous, and well calibrated between theorems and radius-3 conjectures. Minor room for improvement includes detailing the provenance and scope of the cited Lean companion in the text, while radius >= 3 optimality remains open.

ext_10.rationale: The exact logit-gradient derivation (Equation 3) and identical-prompt null control compellingly demonstrate that per-coordinate forward-KL clamping at tau = 1e-6 reverses updates on under-covered tokens and drives support collapse without any privileged content, with exemplary honesty about preregistered criteria missed as worded and missing runs. Weaknesses include an incomplete confirmatory grid (16/18 runs, leaving only two seeds in both exact-KL privileged cells and an unresolved paired-context accuracy contrast), evaluation limited to a single 4B non-thinking model at 4k tokens without testing the proposed sign-preserving fix, and minor imprecisions calling the negative KL terms 'unbounded' (they are bounded below by -1/e) and labeling two-seed exact-KL curves as n=3 in figure legends.

ext_11.rationale: The paper proposes a clever Riemannian tangent-space least-squares algorithm (SIHT) for low-rank Hankel spectral compressed sensing, featuring an exact Krylov parameterization for conjugate gradient and fast 2r x 2r SVD updates that deliver strong empirical speedups. However, the theoretical analysis contains concrete gaps: Theorem 7.2's convergence bound omits a necessary upper bound on the noise norm relative to sigma_min(Gz*), Theorem 4.1(ii) and Section 7.3(ii) lose a factor of r in the noise sample complexity when passing from spectral to Frobenius norm, and Appendix A drops the Hankel penalty term prematurely before invoking LRIP. Furthermore, the theory assumes exact subproblem solves while omitting the inner CG iteration growth needed to sustain quadratic convergence, and experiments test only undamped signals with B = AD^{-1} rather than A Gaussian.

ext_12.rationale: This is a highly rigorous, cleanly written number-theoretic study that classifies sum-balanced cyclic subgroups modulo pq at indices two and four, proving biquadratic exclusion, exact imprimitive quartic moment criteria with limiting proportions 1/4 and 1/2, an infinite conductor-13 family separating sum-balance from Pomerance-Ulmer coset balance, and explicit primitive triangular criteria. Its scholarly grounding, verification (complete analytical proofs, direct numerical witnesses, scoped Lean 4 formalizations, and an exhaustive census up to pq <= 10000), and claim calibration are exemplary. The main limitations are its specialized niche within classical Dirichlet-character methods and a minor expository slip using the term 'eligible' prior to its explanation in Section 5.3.

ext_13.rationale: The manuscript addresses a timely question by separating broad topic concentration from specific-idea overlap in matched isolated-vs-connected agent communities, and exhibits exemplary honesty by declaring its preregistered primary test inconclusive after missingness bounds span zero rather than substituting an exploratory sensitivity. However, severe execution and statistical flaws undermine the empirical findings: treatment-linked generation attrition (14 connected vs 0 isolated failures) and judge-format failures eliminate 40 of 162 planned pairs, a single surviving Phi/ecology seed distorts the conditioned empty-cell-rejection bootstrap and cell-weighted mean, and cross-model comparisons are confounded by 8x token-ceiling disparities. Additionally, primary outcomes rely entirely on LLM judges with no human ground-truth validation (reporting raw percent agreement rather than kappa/F1 on rare binary matches), and key composition-level numerical tables are omitted from the text.

ext_14.rationale: The paper introduces a natural simultaneous generalization P_k of Hall-Paige complete mappings and proves a sharp existence threshold k < p - 1 for all finite groups, an improvement to k = p - 1 for noncyclic homocyclic p-groups via an elegant GL_n(F_p) double-counting argument, and a crisp cyclic p-group obstruction via a Vandermonde polynomial argument over Z_{p^n}, alongside applications to automorphism-generated Latin squares. All main proofs are complete, logically sound, and well-calibrated, candidly noting that Question 1 remains open and that Theorem 6 is already subsumed by [ALS24]. Minor weaknesses include unpolished copy-editing (typos and misnumbered equation cross-references), an unproved two-line reduction claim for Question 1, and an unverified one-sentence GAP remark for Z_7 semidirect Z_3.

ext_15.rationale: This study demonstrates strong experimental hygiene, including exact validation of its fast simulator against a rational-arithmetic oracle on 17,443 transitions, matched hyperparameter tuning, a shuffled-target negative control, measured intervention TV distances, and transparent reporting of borderline bootstrap equivalence after a 2M-resample audit. However, its scientific reach is narrow: the bespoke toy service-control simulator has limited generality, the selected auxiliary weight (0.03) makes the confirmatory auxiliary gradient negligible relative to the policy gradient (and even larger next-observation weights remain weak), and the held-out set includes an exact duplicate of a trained intervention (TV = 0) plus sensor tiers where a memoryless MLP outperforms the GRU. Minor issues include slightly imprecise Bonferroni framing for two-sided 95% intervals, unexplained negative held-out capacity probe R^2 (-0.91), and a discussion focused largely on unpublished cohort preprints rather than deeper RL mechanistic analysis.

ext_16.rationale: Resolves an explicit open problem on two-state universal reversible Turing machines, proves (3, 2) nonexistence, and substantially improves known state-symbol upper bounds (e.g., reducing three-state conversions from O(m^2 n^3) to O(mn^2) and (3, 36654) to (3, 600)) with clean, verified constructions in Section 3.1 (disjoint direction ranges and reverse counting). Rigor and calibration are exemplary: subtle universality conventions (IsUTMStrict vs. IsUTM and trailing-blank decoding) are handled carefully, minimality is explicitly disclaimed, and all results are reported as formalized in Lean 4/Mathlib with standard axioms and cross-checked against published step counts. Minor scope caveats are transparently noted, including that the Section 3.1 conversions assume zero-shifts occur only into halting states and that Theorem 12 uses the stronger universality predicate.

ext_17.rationale: This preregistered empirical audit is cleanly written and unusually transparent about its exclusion deviation, frozen verdicts, and limitations, with consistent arithmetic across Tables 1-5. However, omitting a same-order resampling control leaves both the 4.1% flip rate and the cross-order agreement detector (AUROC 0.695) fundamentally confounded with stochastic sampling noise, and the comparison to a self-verifier spans two different benchmarks. Furthermore, the narrow single-model scope (293 items, three orders), underpowered position test (83 pooled errors from 35 items with non-independent chi-square tests), and unexamined item-level cause of the reversed-order dip limit its scientific significance.

ext_18.rationale: Presents a strong, rigorous set of graph-theoretic results, including a clean Cartesian-product construction (Theorem 2.11) refuting a diameter-at-most-3 question, complete Cartesian-square characterizations for connected chordal and abelian Cayley graphs (Theorems 3.2 and 3.7), and an inventive lattice-determinant bound (Lemma 4.7) toward classifying quartic circulants with well-covered powers. The proofs inspected are mathematically sound and well situated in the literature. Minor weaknesses include delegating small finite verifications (such as the 12-vertex graph in Theorem 2.10 and five cubic circulants) to external scripts rather than short inline checks, omitting an explicit nonzero-determinant note in Lemma 4.7 Case 2, an unclear abstract reference to 'the final conjecture', and recurring macro spacing typos.

ext_19.rationale: Develops a crisp, fully verified structural obstruction theory for block-exchange descent via commuting source projections (Lemma 1, Theorem 3, and exact source-grid DP formula (3)), proves exactness for unary sources (Theorem 4), and constructs sharp counterexamples (Propositions 5-7 and Table 2) ruling out arbitrary, lexicographically extreme, and greedy-separator mask rules. Exposition, literature contextualization, and claim calibration are all high, with open status of general block-exchange descent and Singleton No-Gap clearly stated. Overall impact is moderated by the specialized scope of the problem and the fact that its central motivating conjecture remains open.

ext_20.rationale: Features a well-designed paired experimental framework that separates communication topology from extra samples (IND(2N)) and isolated revision, paired with exemplary preregistration discipline, automated claim-ledger checks, and informative exploratory evidence that communication lowers entropy and raises individual accuracy without improving plurality accuracy. However, the study is severely underpowered for its 2 pp preregistered margin (only 56 items, including 16 puzzles near 90-100% ceiling, yielding roughly +/-8 pp intervals that leave H1 and H2 unresolved even after three draws), and tests only one low-effort model over a single revision round. Crucially, the Table 5 AICc comparison is statistically flawed—combining binomial likelihoods across correlated item-size pairs with an AICc penalty based on n = 5 to 7 grid points (imposing a +20 penalty against 3-parameter models at n = 5)—and the preregistered H4 knee rule fails trivially due to even-vote ties.

ext_21.rationale: This audit is unusually disciplined in claim calibration and computational verification, pairing seed-level contrasts on a held-out 200/800 calibration-evaluation split, reproducing full-panel float64 scores to zero discrepancy, and checking exact neighbor identities via an independent eigendecomposition verifier. However, its scientific contribution is far too narrow for a top-tier journal: it removes only a single leading PC from saved embeddings of three seeds on 1,000 Flickr30k examples, compares against a rank-1 random control removing just 0.27% variance (versus 14.1% for PC1, making it nearly indistinguishable from centering), leaves the +/-1 pp materiality band (~31% of the 3.19 pp raw gap) unmotivated, and omits the declared eigengap diagnostic from the reported tables. Relying on three inaccessible private cohort manuscripts out of seven total references further limits scholarly self-containment and significance.

ext_22.rationale: The manuscript addresses a genuinely significant problem in quantum information theory—exact Renyi-2 entanglement of purification, full tensor-power and heterogeneous-product additivity, and endpoint perturbation stability for symmetric Werner states—with carefully calibrated claims that avoid unproved optimizer-uniqueness or product-ansatz assumptions. Within the evaluated sections, the Choi-state reformulation, real-basis symmetric-subspace compression (Section III), and explicit canonical channel (Section IV) are mathematically sound and algebraically consistent with the stated closed-form formula. Publication readiness is nonetheless held back by pervasive grammatical and typographical errors ('whom introduced', 'Therefor', 'Finall', 'Let define', sentence fragments), missing theorem/lemma environments, and heavy verbosity that spends ten pages on standard Choi duality and subspace restriction before completing even the lower bound.

ext_23.rationale: This is a mathematically rigorous, publication-ready combinatorics manuscript that unifies the generating trees of inversion-sequence classes 207(2) and 207(3) into parallel catalytic systems differing by a single divided-difference term (Proposition 2) and solves 207(3) via an iterated kernel method with careful z-adic convergence proofs (Proposition 3). Every algebraic reduction, affine recurrence (Proposition 1, yielding an O(N^3) algorithm), and rational-factor identity in the evaluated sections is cleanly justified, and the positioning within the inversion-sequence and generating-tree literature is thorough and exact. The only blemishes observed in the text are a minor unresolved cross-reference ('?? of the supplement' in Section 2) and fairly dense exposition in the proof of the four-type succession rule (13).

ext_24.rationale: The central theorem of the manuscript (Theorem 4, claiming S(t) = (-1)^|V(t)| K(t) for Schmitt's Hopf algebra of graphs) is mathematically false: its proof asserts that a(t) = 1 for a tree, whereas a(G) counts all acyclic orientations of G and therefore equals 2^|E(G)| for any forest (already on K_2, Schmitt's antipode is S(K_2) = 2 K_1^2 - K_2 rather than K_1^2 - K_2). Additional technical flaws appear in Sections 2-4, including reversing the set-difference exponent in Eq. (18) (making it identically +1 for A subset of B), inconsistent poset orientation between Section 3.1 and Figure 1(a), mislabeling spanning subforests as proper subforests, undefined symbols, and an unbridged conceptual gap between the edge-deletion poset and Schmitt's induced-subgraph coproduct. Although auxiliary identities such as Proposition 2 and K^2 = id hold, the fatal error in the core Hopf-algebraic identification precludes publication.

ext_25.rationale: This concise, lucidly written paper makes a strong contribution to spectral graph theory by classifying connected graphs with distance spectrum {rho, 0, -c} for c <= 3 (Theorem 1.1), characterizing the transmission-regular case for smallest distance eigenvalue -3 (Proposition 1.2), and disproving the natural transmission-regularity heuristic via two sporadic Seidel-switched graphs G_36 and G_55 proved unique within equitable switches of SRGs with smallest eigenvalue -2 (Theorem 1.3). All algebraic, interlacing, rank-minor, and inductive proofs are airtight and cleanly presented, supported by an informative geometric figure and exact spectral tables. The main minor weakness is that Theorem 1.1(c) depends critically on a computer search up to n = 19 (Claim 1) whose code and 3,931-graph dataset are only 'available upon request' rather than archived publicly, alongside a slight wording imprecision about alternating signs for positive semidefiniteness when zero is an eigenvalue.

ext_26.rationale: The manuscript presents a mathematically accurate and physically well-motivated hybrid qubit-qumode formulation of (1+1)D lattice Yukawa scattering and decay on trapped ions, with verified normal-mode Bogoliubov transformations, exact lattice leading-order width with group-velocity factor, native Trotter gate compilation (including exact parity cancellation of odd-mode unconditional displacements), and a coherent-subtracted Gaussian readout scheme. Its claims are well calibrated regarding N^2 interaction-gate and N(N-1)/2 beam-splitter scaling, hardware-versus-MPS state preparation, and apples-to-apples lattice RPA/NLO benchmarking. Minor caveats in the visible text include an unstated Jordan-Wigner phase gauge in Eq. (11) and an idealized blue-sideband single-phonon preparation step assuming the displaced interacting vacuum approximates the Fock vacuum, while the numerical emulation results themselves lie beyond the truncated window.

ext_27.rationale: The experiment exhibits disciplined preregistration, exact count-coupled masking, verified endpoint arithmetic, and admirably restrained claims that carefully rule out retention gains, ordinary-training superiority, or full VSD replication. However, its scientific significance is narrow—testing standard argmax hard-example selection on a 192-item synthetic single-token memorization task in a 135M model where correctness gating essentially ties ordinary training (66.93% vs 66.63% joint)—and it overlooks a major analytical confound: the uniform scalar control recovers roughly 85% of the joint-accuracy gap over random selection (64.81% vs 52.88%) with a smaller step-norm sum, indicating that sparse random-subset variance rather than hard-example identity drives most of the primary effect. Moreover, five of nine references are inaccessible private cohort preprints (which also hold the task specification and parent checkpoints), leaving key continual-learning and online-batch-selection literature unaddressed and the paper non-self-contained.

ext_28.rationale: This manuscript delivers clean, self-contained constructive proofs for a cyclic two-qutrit family under collective dephasing—combining explicit finite product decompositions, realignment and cyclic Choi witnesses, closed-form time-invariant negativity, and one-copy distillability—and makes a sharp observation showing via an explicit negative 3x3 partial-transpose determinant that the printed global dephasing channel entangles product inputs. However, Eq. (17) contains a genuine error: applying (D_kl tensor D_kl) rather than (D_kl tensor D_kl*) annihilates the off-diagonals of H_0 and preserves C_sw, reversing the stated action of the local random-unitary channel. In addition, the static separability classification is an acknowledged specialization of prior cyclic-sign-invariant results, the sweeping claim that prior distillability-sudden-death studies always ended in separability is insufficiently substantiated, and the prose contains numerous typos and grammatical slips.

ext_29.rationale: The study exemplifies transparent preregistered reporting, cleanly separating confirmatory from exploratory analyses, documenting deviations D1-D3, reporting the held-back 719-problem non-replication (0.0 pp), and highlighting that training-seed variance dominates test-sampling noise. Its publication readiness for a top-tier venue is limited by an inconclusive, underpowered primary test (m=3 seeds, t_2 interval [-6.3, +3.2] pp), anti-conservative three-seed bootstrap CIs without t_2 intervals on within-arm contrasts, an incomplete factorial design (missing the standard replace+restart cell and reducing accumulate+continue to one seed), and the lack of temperature- or entropy-matched evaluation to separate genuine coverage loss from distribution sharpening. Scope is further constrained to one 0.8B model on GSM8K, and the related-work discussion relies partly on inaccessible private cohort preprints and an informal room message.

ext_30.rationale: This manuscript settles an established open conjecture on bipartite subadditivity of subentropy across the entire Nichols-Wootters family in a common ambient dimension, completely resolves strong subadditivity failure (including exact +/- 1/12 quantum Markov defects), obtains optimal two-qubit constants (1/3 for subentropy and 2/3 for S_2^(4) and S_3^(4)), and establishes a novel operational classical-capacity interpretation. Every identity in the visible introduction and preliminaries—including the contour and simplex formulas, zero-padding recursion, the positive Stiefel compression representation (Proposition 2.2), and the adapted Bregman divergence (Proposition 2.4)—verifies cleanly, with rigorous calibration of the common-dimension requirement and clear credit to prior structural results. Only minor presentation issues appear in the excerpt (a slight log/ln inconsistency and monograph-scale length), while full verification of the downstream Section 4-5 and Appendix proofs lies beyond the evaluation window.
